title: Lantern Craft and Candle Play
strapline: Tissue-paper lanterns with a safe little candle inside — the same idea, found in celebration after celebration.
intent: Children explore how lanterns and candles are used across Diwali, Hanukkah, Christmas and birthdays.
Children begin to grasp that light is a shared symbol, used differently by different families.
Cutting, sticking and wrapping tissue paper builds design and making skills.
Battery candles let children handle "flame" safely and talk about real fire safety.
Seeing their own lantern lit gives an immediate, visible reward for the making.
implementation: Provide card, tissue paper, foil and glue so children can build and cover a lantern.
Keep the structure simple enough that the child does the work, not the adult.
Offer battery-operated tea lights to place inside — never a real flame.
Talk about the different celebrations that use lanterns and candles as the children work.
Demonstrate safe handling and talk honestly about why real candles are dangerous.
Support cutting and sticking without taking the scissors out of their hands.
Display the lit lanterns in a dimmed corner so the effect is properly visible.
key_questions: How will the light get out of your lantern?
What happens when you hold the tissue paper up to the light?
Which celebrations can you think of that use candles?
Why do we use a pretend candle instead of a real one?
How is your lantern different from your friend's?

impact.text: Children know that families, faiths and ways of living vary, and find that interesting.
Children cut, stick and assemble with intent and growing precision.
Children create with a plan and adapt when the materials misbehave.
Children talk about their own creation and notice detail in others'.
Children explore how light passes through materials and changes them.
Children ask real questions about fire, light and safety and expect real answers.

enhancements: A lantern parade around the setting at the end of the day in winter dark.
A light-box table where lanterns and translucent materials can be tested.
A comparison shelf of real lanterns borrowed from families who celebrate.
A colour-mixing investigation using overlapping tissue paper.
A story about a festival of light kept alongside the making table.
A shadow-and-silhouette extension using the lit lanterns against a wall.

playing_exploring: Children test how different papers let light through before choosing.
The making is open-ended — no two lanterns need look alike.
active_learning: Children stay with a fiddly construction until it stands up and works.
The moment of lighting it rewards the persistence directly.
creating_thinking: Children plan a lantern and solve the problem of getting light out of it.
They connect their lantern to celebrations they know and ones they have just met.
